name: Globe artichoke

schedule.notes: Annual varieties (Imperial Star) crop in year 1. Perennial types need 2 weeks of <50 F to trigger bud set ('vernalization').
Light frost actually helps — exposes seedlings to the cold they need for budding.
Heavy feeder. Compost top-dress every 4 to 6 weeks.
Cut buds with 2 in of stem when tight; leaves on the bud begin to flare = past prime.

harvest.cues: Buds are fist-sized, tight, scales pressed close. Outer scales beginning to flare = harvest now or it's too late.
harvest.storageNotes: Fridge in plastic 1 week. Stems in a glass of water also work. Buds left to flower produce huge purple thistle blooms (great cut flower) but no more food.

varieties.name: Imperial Star
varieties.notes: Bred to crop in year 1 without vernalization. The choice for zones 6 and below.

varieties.name: Green Globe
varieties.notes: Classic perennial in zones 7+. Crops for 4 to 6 years before replacement.

notes: Dramatic 3 to 4 ft silver-green plants — earn their space even without buds. Below zone 7, mulch heavily for winter or grow as an annual. Each plant gives 6 to 12 buds in a good year.
